sentences.text: Respondent :- Adjudicating Officer / Additional District Magistrate And Another Counsel for Appellant :- Suneel Kumar Rai Hon'ble Dr. Kaushal Jayendra Thaker,J.
I have heard learned counsel for appellant and learned Standing Counsel for State.

This appeal has been preferred against the order dated 28.11.2019 passed by District Judge, Aligarh in Misc. Civil Appeal No. 85 of 2019 dismissing the appeal under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.
Brief facts giving rise to the present appeal is that appellant is a seller fruits at the road side of Sarsaul, Aligarh.
On 15.10.2016 He was falsely implicated by the respondent no.2 on the allegations of ripening banana by applying chemical.
Sample of the fruit was sent to Food Analytic, Lucknow and after getting report therefrom, a Case No. 38 of 2017 was registered before respondent no.1.

Appellant filed his objection to the notice issued to him but, according to the appellant, without considering his reply an order was passed by the respondent no.1 on 26.8.2019 imposing a penalty of Rs.5,00,000/- against the appellant under Section 57(1)(ii) of Food Safety and Standard Act,
2006.

Dissatisfied with the said order, appellant filed Appeal No. 85 of 2009 before the Tribunal,
which was dismissed by the Tribunal as not pressed on 28.11.2019 without considering the facts and Dilshad vs Adjudicating Officer / Additional ... on 31 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76889901/
1 circumstances.
Regard being had to the facts and submissions, I am of the view that the appeal no. 85 of 2019 ought not to have been dismissed in such a cursory manner.
As such, the appellant is permitted to amend the said appeal memo also by arraying appropriate parties as according to him, he is only seller and not purchaser of the goods.
With these observations, the appeal is allowed without going into the merits of the case.
Order impugned in this appeal is quashed.
